text: This is an AI narration over real screen recordings of Skuld running. Nothing on screen is mocked, animated, or sped up.
In Moo-joe-co, a Franka Panda pushes a block into a target region. This classical controller passes its nominal test three times, bit for bit identical. Would you ship it?

Skuld perturbs four physical variables: block offset, mass, friction and observation delay. Same budget of twenty-five episodes: random testing found three failures, the first at episode sixteen. Active search found six, the first at episode six, and closer to nominal.

The first failure random search found: delay one hundred fifty-two milliseconds, mass and friction raised. A deterministic oracle reads simulator state and applies the rule never collision. The finger touched the floor at three and a half seconds. No model decides this.

The minimizer reverts offset, mass and friction one at a time; the failure survives each revert. One variable remains: one hundred forty milliseconds of observation delay. Three replays, byte identical, stored as a regression test.
A live Tavily search pulled the manufacturer's three kilogram payload figure. It became a constraint only after a human approved it; name and timestamp are in the record.

Nemotron, an NVIDIA model on Nebius Token Factory, proposed the constraint and a hypothesis. Its first quote was not verbatim, so the validator refused it and kept the rejection. The accepted hypothesis ran in simulation: finger on the floor. The model proposes; physics decides.

The release gate blocks version one on its stored counterexample and on two held-out cases it never searched. A repaired version two is eligible: it passed the named simulation suite, which never means safe. Nine injected faults, from missing telemetry to corrupt artifacts, all fail closed.
Same budget, same oracle: active search found closer failures than random. The next round broke version two again at one hundred eighty-two milliseconds. That is the next regression test.
Skuld. What your robot policy owes before it ships.
